issues.description: SealSaloon.checkOrderReady is specified in the problem statement/UML as a no-argument method `checkOrderReady(): void`, but the solution defines `checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging)` instead. This changes the required public API and can break tests or student implementations that follow the specification and expect/call the no-arg method.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide the required `public void checkOrderReady()` method matching the specification and have `orderMeal` call it. If optional logging is desired, keep `checkOrderReady(boolean)` as a private helper and delegate from the public no-arg method.

issues.description: The UML lists only Stock methods add/take/findStockIngredient/addToStockIngredients/emptyStock, but both template and solution expose an additional public method `setStockIngredients(StockIngredient[])`. This extra public API is not described in the specification and may lead students to rely on a method that is not intended to be part of the exercise design.
issues.suggestedFix: Either remove `public void setStockIngredients(...)` (and adjust any demo usage) to match the UML, or update the UML/problem statement to explicitly include this setter if it is intended to be part of the required API.

issues.description: The problem statement is internally inconsistent about the `stock` field in SealSaloon: it first describes `stock` as a `final Stock` instance attribute initialized in the constructor, but later requires `stock` to be static (shared across all instances). This ambiguity can mislead students about whether `stock` should be instance-level or class-level.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent by choosing one design: (A) specify `stock` as `static final Stock stock` everywhere (including UML notation), or (B) specify it as an instance `final Stock stock` and remove the requirement that it must be static/shared.
